correctness.rationale: Restricting the published four-collinear determinant to the baseline gives the exact bracket identity \((v_1-v_4)(v_2-v_3)[13][24]-(v_1-v_3)(v_2-v_4)[14][23]\), which on an affine chart is precisely equality of source and target cross ratios. Every diagonal projective transform therefore lies on the divisor; both its orbit closure and the irreducible divisor have dimension three, so they coincide. The affine equation is a quadratic form in the four target coordinates. Independent symbolic computation for distinct source coordinates gives Hessian rank three, kernel spanned by the common-shift vector, and every principal 3-by-3 minor equal to twice the nonzero Vandermonde. Hence the affine singular locus is exactly the diagonal and the normal quadratic form is nondegenerate. Simultaneous projective changes move any target quadruple into an affine chart, making the statement global. A rank-three quadratic is irreducible; the hypersurface is Cohen--Macaulay and its one-dimensional singular locus has codimension two in the threefold, so Serre's criterion gives normality. Because the defining equation is exactly quadratic transverse to the diagonal, the local analytic germ is \(A_1\).
